findings.label: def:p09-ctmc-csl
findings.claim: Replacing arbitrary nonempty rational-endpoint CSL interval I by its closure does not change path probability.
findings.counterexample: Use singleton state s, R(s,s)=0 (absorbing), and p true at s. Let false abbreviate neg top. Then (neg top) U^(0,1] p is false on its constant absorbing trajectory: every t>0 demands neg top at u=0. Its probability is0. For closure[0,1], t=0 is a witness and the earlier-time condition is empty, so (neg top) U^[0,1] p has probability1.
findings.evidence: Actual timed-until clause at1377–1380; absorbing/final-path clauses at1331–1345.
findings.precise_remaining: Remove or correctly restrict the blanket endpoint-closure assertion, preserving interval flags and the t=0 until case. Any more general endpoint theorem requires its hypotheses and proof.
findings.source_attribution: This is a defect in the current host assertion as written. The cited Baier–Haverkort–Hermanns–Katoen paper was not re-read here; no source-error claim is made.
findings.relationship: Same already recorded NEW-P9-CSL-INTERVAL-CLOSURE; counted once, not a new second defect.
